 42m ago 09.42 EDT Will Unwin Match report: Aston Villa 2-1 Man City 
 Manchester City have added a loss in the Premier League to the one to the Premier League, as their perfect on-pitch record vanished at Aston Villa. The two most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side come out on top against Erling Haaland.
 City are certainly infallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost them as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma played their part in Jackson’s goals, which will give him greater pleasure as they ended Enzo Maresca’s perfect start.
 Aston Villa and Jackson end Manchester City’s perfect run with stunning win Read more Share 45m ago 09.39 EDT Matty Cash’s verdict
 double quotation mark As a team I think we were amazing. We’ve tried to make Villa Park a fortress in the last few years and I think we’ve done that.
 [On Unai Emery] He’s just a tactical genius. You have to adapt against top teams and he’s always coming up with new ideas.
 [On his tactics against Jeremy Doku] It was an individual decision. I do a lot of work on wingers and how I can stop them. I watched a lot of clips of Doku, and for me the best way was to get tight and be aggressive. You can’t do it all the time, of course, but I thought I did well today. When he turns and faces, he’s one of the best in the world.
 [On Zion Suzuki] When he came in, I thought we’d signed a midfielder! Sometimes he shapes to play it to one full-back and then reverse it to the other. I’m like, ‘I’m not ready for this!’ The other thing he does so well is come for crosses, which is a dream for a full-back.
 Share Updated at  09.40 EDT 53m ago 09.31 EDT “Just imagine how good Villa might be,” says Eddy Nason, “if they started the season in August rather than mid-September!”
 Quite. Villa had one point (and one goal) after four Premier League games. Now they have 11 points from eight matches, plus nine from three in the Champions League.
 Share 1h ago 09.27 EDT Nicolas Jackson’s reaction
 double quotation mark [On his matchwinning performance as a lone striker] It’s my work so I’m very happy to do it. Hopefully I’ll be injury-free and I can keep on doing it.
 I know the coach [from Villarreal]. He’s an incredible manager and we have an incredible dressing-room. Hopefully I’ll score many goals for them.
 Share 1h ago 09.26 EDT The final whistle brings a mighty roar from the Villa fans, who must be so damn proud of their football team and especially their outstanding manager.
 Unai Emery has mastermined a stirring victory against a City team who had won seven out of seven. City contributed fully to a fabulous game, but you’d need a plastic banana to begrudge Villa the three points.
 Share Updated at  09.28 EDT 1h ago 09.23 EDT Full time: Aston Villa 2-1 Man City
 Unai Emery is a boss .
 Share 1h ago 09.23 EDT 90+5 min Buendia is booked for a foul on Lewis, and there’s a brief bit of nonsense on the touchline involving some of the coaches.
 Share 1h ago 09.22 EDT 90+4 min Khusanov commits a witless foul on Madjo, allowing Villa to eat up another 30 seconds.
 Share 1h ago 09.21 EDT 90+2 min Two minutes left for City to save the game. An angled, driven cross from deep on the left is headed towards goal by Haaland and saved comfortably by Suzuki. Torres did well to ensure Haaland couldn’t get a clear header.
 Share 1h ago 09.19 EDT 90+1 min An overhit cross from the teenager McAidoo gives Villa a goalkick.
 Share 1h ago 09.19 EDT 90 min Four minutes of added time. Two-hundred and forty seconds.
 Share 1h ago 09.18 EDT 89 min Foden dances to the byline on the left and lifts a deep cross towards Haaland, whose powerful header is nodded clear by Maatsen in the six-yard box. Suzuki might have had it covered, I’m not sure. But it was excellent defending and Maatsen has improved hugely in the second half.
 Moments later, Doku screws a difficult volley well wide.
 Share 1h ago 09.15 EDT 86 min After an extended spell of City possession, Foden spanks a rising drive from 25 yards that is blocked by Cash.
 Right now, City don’t look like scoring. But then nor did Villa at 1-1.
 Share 1h ago 09.13 EDT 84 min “Win, lose or draw today, I’ll raise a glass of rosé to the best pound for pound manager in the Prem today,” says Mike Daniels. “Unai is the man.”
 Good evening email.
 Share 1h ago 09.13 EDT 83 min Within seconds of coming on, Madjo is booked for kicking the ball away. This is his Premier League debut, but I don’t thnk that’s a record – wasn’t Myles Lewis-Skelly booked before making his debut at Manchester City in 2024-25?
 Share 1h ago 09.10 EDT 82 min: Double substitution Leon Goretzka and Brian Madjo replace Joao Gomes, who was excellent, and Nicolas Jackson, who was quite outstanding.
 Share Updated at  09.11 EDT 1h ago 09.10 EDT 81 min Lots of City possession, but Villa are keeping them at arm’s length. They were hanging on when Jackson put them 2-1 ahead; since then they’ve been a lot more comfortable.
 Share Updated at  09.11 EDT 1h ago 09.07 EDT 78 min McAidoo breaks the lines and plays a simple ball to the overlapping Lewis. His cross is wildly overhit and that’s the end of that.
 Share 1h ago 09.05 EDT 77 min Doku, under pressure from Cash, heads the ball out of play. Doku has had some dangerous moments – he’s too good not to – but overall Cash has played him well.
 Share Updated at  09.06 EDT 1h ago 09.05 EDT 76 min The first signs of frustration from City, who haven’t put Villa under sustained pressure since going 2-1 behind.
 As I type that, McAidoo is booked for a cynical foul on Maatsen.
 Share 1h ago 09.02 EDT 74 min Anderson leaves one on Joao Gomes and is booked.
 Share 1h ago 09.00 EDT 72 min McAidoo feeds the underlapping Lewis, whose cutback towards Foden is read and intercepted by Kamara. A quietly brilliant piece of defending.
 Share 1h ago 08.58 EDT 69 min: Man City substitution Ryan McAidoo replaces Iliman Ndiaye.
 Share 1h ago 08.57 EDT 68 min: Superb save by Suzuki!
 Doku’s ball across the area hits a Villa defender and ricochets towards goal. Gvardiol is first to the loose ball but Suzuki flies off his line to smother his shot. Brilliant anticipation from Suzuki.
 View image in fullscreen Top work from Zion Suzuki. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters Share Updated at  09.00 EDT 1h ago 08.55 EDT 66 min: Villa substitution Emi Buendia and Ross Barkley on, Johan Manzambi and the outstanding John McGinn off.
 Share 2h ago 08.53 EDT 65 min Fernandez’s orner is headed back across goal and well wide by Gvardiol. Half a chance.
 Share 2h ago 08.53 EDT 65 min “I must say, I think not enough is made of the principled stand of Manchester City fans during this whole boosted revenue escapade/debacle,” says Paul Griffin. “Their decision to wave bananas – inflated, artificial and completely implausible – is admirable.”
 Share 2h ago 08.53 EDT 63 min Nicolas Jackson has given a lone-striker masterclass today.
 Share 2h ago 08.51 EDT It’s a mistake from Gianluigi Donnarumma, but Villa worked the ball so well. Jackson turned brilliantly on the halfway line, swept the ball out to Mbaye on the right and got on his bike.
 Mbaye ran at a backpedalling defender before arrowing a low pass back towards Jackson on the edge of the area. He swept a first-time shot on the run that went through Donnarumma and into the net.
 It was straight at Donnarumma, and a playground goalkeeper would have cleared it nonchalantly with their right foot. But Donnarumma’s goalkeeping instinct kicked in; he tried to save it with his hands, couldn’t contort his body as required and pushed the ball into the net.
 Share Updated at  08.56 EDT 2h ago 08.48 EDT GOAL! Aston Villa 2-1 Man City (Jackson 60)
 Ibrahim Mbaye has made a goal within seconds of coming on!
 View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson scores again for Villa! Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters View image in fullscreen Photograph: Ed Sykes/Apl/Sportsphoto Share Updated at  08.56 EDT 2h ago 08.48 EDT 60 min: Villa substitution Ibrahim Mbaye is on for Alysson.
 Share 2h ago 08.48 EDT 59 min Doku curls wide from distance after a trademark run infield.
 Share 2h ago 08.48 EDT 58 min A ferocious clearance from Khusanov hits Manzanbi in a very personal space. He falls over, then rolls off the field in serious pain.
 It’s a very cold day, so I feel Manzanbi’s pain, but at least they’re not playing with a Mitre Mouldmaster.
 Share Updated at  08.53 EDT 2h ago 08.45 EDT 57 min Incidentally, Haaland has now scored 13 goals in his last nine games. And that’s without any hat-tricks.
 Share 2h ago 08.45 EDT 56 min: Good save by Suzuki! Doku cuts inside from the left and fires an angled pass into the underlapping Gvardiol. He takes the ball in his stride like a seasoned No10 and whacks a rising drive that is pushed over well by Suzuki.
 Share Updated at  08.46 EDT 2h ago 08.44 EDT 55 min Now Cash is booked for a poor – possibly accidental – tackle on Doku. His studs went into the back of Doku’s foot, probably just below the achilles.
 Share 2h ago 08.43 EDT 54 min Manzanbi is booked for delaying a City restart. Villa are on the ropes.
 Share 2h ago 08.42 EDT A clinical finish from Erling Haaland brings City level . Ndiaye, who has been excellent on the right, beat Manzanbi with a stepover and clipped an inviting cross to the far post. Haaland got up early, ahead of Lindelof, and slammed a downward header into the net from six yards.
 Share 2h ago 08.41 EDT GOAL! Aston Villa 1-1 Man City (Haaland 52)
 See 48 min.
 View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland heads Manchester City level! Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA View image in fullscreen Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters Share Updated at  08.45 EDT 2h ago 08.39 EDT 50 min A promising City attack ends when Anderson overhits a cross from the De Bruyne Zone. He normally measures his crosses expertly from that position. On this occasion, the ball flies out of play and the home fans whistle with disdain.
 Share Updated at  08.40 EDT 2h ago 08.38 EDT 48 min That header, by the way, was only Haaland’s ninth touch of the game. It’s the tenth, eleventh and twelfth that Villa will be worried about.
 Share 2h ago 08.36 EDT 47 min Villa break after an errant pass from Lewis. Eventually Maatsen pings a shot that ricochets behind for a corner. Cash takes, Haaland wins it in the air and City eventually clear.
 Share 2h ago 08.35 EDT 46 min Back under way. Khusanov has moved infield to centre-back.
 Share 2h ago 08.34 EDT Half-time substitutions
 Manchester City have brought on Phil Foden and Rico Lewis for Marc Guehi and Rayan Cherki.
 Share 2h ago 08.22 EDT Half-time reading 
 I’m looking forward to Older and Calmer, a duet between Jose and Indigo De Souza .
 Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico Read more Share 2h ago 08.21 EDT Half time: Aston Villa 1-0 Man City
 A raw, compelling first half at Villa Park. Nicolas Jackson’s early goal capped a ferocious start from Villa – who had more than 90% of the possession at that stage – and set up a fascinating clash of styles.
 City dominated the ball for the rest of the half: the impressive Iliman Ndiaye hit the post and was one of two City players to have penalty appeals turned down. But Villa, with Jackson and John McGinn outstanding, were a constant menace in transition.
 In short: cracking game, more please!
 Share 2h ago 08.18 EDT 45 min One minute of added time. Cherki’s curving pass towards Haaland is cut out by the last defender Lindelof. There was a lot of grass behind Lindelof but Cherki didn’t quite get the pass right.
 Share 2h ago 08.17 EDT 44 min Ndiaye’s deflected cross is claimed at the second attempt by Suzuki. City’s wide players have been a big threat.
 Share 2h ago 08.14 EDT 42 min Pound for pound, Unai Emery is the best manager in the world: discuss.
 (I don’t know whether I think this, but it’s surely up for discussion. It’s astonishing that he has them playing this well so soon after losing Martinez, Konsa, Digne, Rogers, Tielemans, Rogers, Watkins.)
 Share 2h ago 08.12 EDT 40 min: Great tackle by Dias!
 Alysson moves elegantly into the area from the right, hugging the ball on his left foot. He zig-zags between Dias and another City player and is about to shoot – probably score – when Dias makes a fabulous recovery tackle.
 Share 2h ago 08.11 EDT 38 min Cherki loses the ball to Manzanbi, pulls him back to stop a Villa break and is booked. Villa have kept Cherki very quiet in his day job.
 Share 2h ago 08.09 EDT 37 min There’s a cracking atmosphere at Villa Park: constant hostility from the home fans, period defiance from the away end.
 Another good run from Doku leads to a City corner. Enzo Fernandez takes, Kamara heads away at the near post.
 Share 2h ago 08.06 EDT 34 min … and Manzanbi whacks it over the bar. A poor effort by his standards.
 Share 2h ago 08.06 EDT 33 min The free-kick is just outside the area, slightly to the left of centre…
 Share Updated at  08.06 EDT 2h ago 08.05 EDT 32 min Guehi is booked for fouling Jackson just outside the area. It was a bit of a wrestling match, and Guehi didn’t think he’d committed the foul. The home fans, by contrast, thought it should have been a Dogso red card. I’m pretty sure there was a covering defender.
 With Villa seeing very little of the ball in the last 25 minutes, Nicolas Jackson has been fantastic .
 Share 2h ago 08.04 EDT 31 min Now City want a penalty when Maatsen, who is really struggling, misses a lunging tackle at Ndiaye, who then goes over. Hard to tell whether he was fouled or whether he slipped. It was clumsy from Maatsen but it’s been cleared by VAR.
 View image in fullscreen Iliman Ndiaye is up-ended by Ian Maatsen. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  08.08 EDT 2h ago 08.03 EDT 31 min “I’ve come late to the MBM and need to warn you not to put ideas into people’s heads,” writes Richard Hirst. “At the rate Man City are collecting points a 50 point deduction would be nowhere near enough to ensure that they finish below Fulham.”
 Share 2h ago 08.02 EDT 30 min Manzanbi goes over in the area after running into Anderson. The Villa fans want a penalty but the referee isn’t interested; nor are VAR. It looked like Anderson just stood his ground.
